name: T-Bar Row
description: The T-bar row is a horizontal pulling exercise in which one end of a barbell is anchored and the loaded end is rowed toward the chest in a bent-over position. The angled bar path and neutral or close grip emphasize the mid-back and lats, and the fixed anchor allows for significant loading with relatively lower spinal stress than a free barbell row.

execution.starting_position: Stand astride the barbell with one end anchored. Hinge at the hips to approximately 45 degrees with a neutral spine. Grip the close-grip handle or the bar itself just inside the loaded end.
execution.setup_instructions: Place a landmine anchor (or wedge a barbell into a corner). Attach weight plates to the free end. Use a close-grip attachment or a V-bar over the bar if available.
steps: With a braced core and hinged position, row the barbell toward your chest.
Drive the elbows behind the torso and squeeze the mid-back at the peak.
Lower under control until the arms are fully extended.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the row, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Standing too upright, reducing back activation
Using momentum by bobbing the torso up and down
safety_considerations: Maintain a neutral spine — do not round the lower back under heavy load
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension at the bottom, plates touch or near-touch the chest at the top.
coaching_cues: Hinge like a hinge door — keep the angle consistent
Squeeze your back like you are cracking a walnut between your shoulder blades
